subject.title: macOS launchd: plugin/config maintenance can leave Control UI in broken partial-reload state; restart may require doctor --fix

question: Should Gateway partial reloads become a shared degraded-state contract for session RPCs and Control UI, or should this stay limited to narrower WebChat recovery notices and operator guidance?
rationale: The code already has probes, startup-gated methods, restart deferral, and stale PID cleanup, but deciding whether `sessions.resolve` should stop returning ordinary missing-session errors during partial reloads changes the user-visible runtime contract across Gateway, Control UI, and recovery.

options.title: Define A Shared Degraded-State Contract
options.body: Make reload/readiness state explicit in Gateway RPCs and Control UI, including `sessions.resolve`, and validate the macOS launchd maintenance path end to end.

options.title: Land Only Narrow WebChat Notice Work
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95154 as the immediate subset fix and leave broader partial-reload behavior for later reports.

options.title: Document Operator Maintenance Limits
options.body: Accept that live plugin/config maintenance can temporarily break user sessions and focus only on clearer docs and diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Define A Shared Degraded-State Contract
recommendation.body: Make reload/readiness state explicit in Gateway RPCs and Control UI, including `sessions.resolve`, and validate the macOS launchd maintenance path end to end.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across gateway runtime, readiness, sessions, and macOS service recovery areas where this history points most strongly.
